messages:
maria: Heads-up — charts on /orgs/:id/metrics stutter on interaction after today's deploy. Repro: open org metrics, switch range to 1h, hover a point. Chrome: frames drop, spinner appears, then chart jumps. Seen on mac + linux.

tsai: Ugh. Any perf traces or console errors? Which build/hash?

maria: repro trace attached (running locally): https://perf.internal/trace/xyz789. Build: 2026.03.18-4501. No uncaught errors, just long frame times and repeated network calls.

devon: Flamegraph looks bad — long tasks from computeLayout + updateSeries. Telemetry show longtask count per interaction went 0.2 -> 1.2s and JS heap delta +30MB on range switch. Also seeing repeated identical GETs to /api/v1/metrics/series with x-cache: MISS.

devon: logs (snip):
```
GET /api/v1/metrics/series?prefix=cpu&start=1678980000&end=1678983600
200 34ms x-cache: MISS
GET /api/v1/metrics/series?prefix=cpu&start=1678980000&end=1678983600
200 36ms x-cache: MISS
GET /api/v1/metrics/series?prefix=cpu&start=1678980000&end=1678983600
200 35ms x-cache: MISS
```

olivia: I ran a bundle diff against the last green and saw +48KB in the charting chunk; commit 8f9a2 pulled in a tiny time helper and a cache-key normalization change. The helper itself shouldn't spike long tasks. The cache-key change added tzOffset into the key: if the client hydrates with undefined tz then later patches it, key changes and we always MISS.

maria: Where is tz injected? We set tz from userPrefs and then client sends it on first render — looks like hydration order is causing inconsistent keys. That would explain repeated identical GETs from the same session.

sam: Quick mitigation ideas: debounce range updates on the chart UI and memoize the computed cache key until hydrate completes. Add a guard where tz is normalized to a stable default (UTC) until prefs are available.

tsai: We should also add telemetry to detect this class of regressions: increment cache.prefix_miss metric when response has x-cache: MISS and tag with route=/metrics/series + user_agent. And emit longtask_count on range-change events.

devon: I can open a PR with: memoize cache key, debounce range input (200ms), add telemetry increment, plus an e2e smoke check ensuring x-cache becomes HIT for repeated requests after first fetch. Plan to cut a canary. Anyone want to pair on tests? :eyes:

olivia: I'll review the PR — also add a defensive check so we don't include tz in the key until userPrefs.ready === true. That should avoid key churn during hydrate.

maria: Sounds good. For rollout UX: let's canary at 10% for 30m then 50% if no regressions in longtask/heap/latency. I can watch dashboard and flip the rollback if needed. :shipit:

devon: Steps I'll take now:
- branch chart-cache-fix
- implement memoize + debounce + telemetry
- add e2e smoke and unit for key normalization
- open PR and request review from @olivia and @maria
- deploy canary via console rollouts 10%

tsai: Also add an alert rule: if longtask_p95 > 600ms OR cache.prefix_miss_rate > 0.3 for console-frontend, page rollback.

maria: Good call. Add a dashboard panel showing cache_miss_rate and longtask_95 for the last 1h so we can MTTR.

deploy-bot: Started deploy of chart-cache-fix canary to service 'console-frontend' (canary 10%) — build 2026.03.18-4567. Link: https://deploys.internal/console-frontend/2026.03.18-4567

maria: Watching metrics now. If anyone sees regressions ping here and I'll pause the canary. :eyes:
